meta.merged_note: The audit ran on `audit/2026-09-18` off base dbba4df. The work was fast-forwarded onto main and pushed; the remote had one commit the branch did not (d15a56b, an automated badge refresh of .github/traffic.json), so main was rebased onto it before the push. Rebasing changed only parentage: `git diff --name-only ca9c2e6 bc3edc0` prints only .github/traffic.json, so every file the verification reads is byte-identical. ca9c2e6 is the commit Phase E verified; bc3edc0 is its rebased equivalent and is what the task commit fields below name.

tasks.title: Prototype split dbba4df dropped four runtime imports, so the 3D walkthrough cannot start
tasks.discovered_by: eslint no-undef + git show dbba4df^ + node repro + subagent
tasks.evidence_before: dbba4df re-added THREE but not RoomEnvironment (scene-building.js:88), SG_LON/SG_LAT/SG_UTC_OFFSET (sun.js:17/19/33), seedFromString (scene-building-3.js:239) or playPlop (paintball.js:20). Each is a ReferenceError on the normal 3D path: start() is caught and shows '3D failed to start: RoomEnvironment is not defined'; applyTimeOfDay() throws out of store.emit(); syncCity() aborts the build; every paintball shot throws. Reproduced each with node against the real modules. `./tests/run.sh --fast` is green (31 files, 1492 assertions) while 3D is dead.
tasks.fix_summary: Restored RoomEnvironment (scene-building.js), SG_LAT/SG_LON/SG_UTC_OFFSET (sun.js), seedFromString (scene-building-3.js) and playPlop (paintball.js); start() disposes the RoomEnvironment it builds.
tasks.evidence_after: node tests/audit-walk3d.test.mjs 78/0 (7 passed / 45 failed before); three-environment 105/0; ./tests/run.sh --fast 37 files / 1824 assertions / 0 failed.

tasks.title: sanitize() is not total on a malformed document: five dereference sites throw a TypeError and the whole room is lost
tasks.discovered_by: manual Tier A read + node repro + subagent
tasks.evidence_before: Proven with node: walls:[null] / [{}] / a wall with no start -> TypeError at sanitize.js:155 via wallLength (walls.js:13); furniture with a known kind but no/null center -> TypeError at 282; publicAreas:[null] -> TypeError at 289; canvas/origin as a truthy primitive -> TypeError at 107/121 (ES modules are strict). sanitize.js:266-272 states in its own words that losing the whole document over one bad field 'is the one failure a repair pass must not have'.
tasks.fix_summary: sanitize() guards every unvalidated dereference (walls, furniture center, publicAreas, primitive canvas/origin), drops-and-reports what it cannot use, and core.js gains isRecord().
tasks.evidence_after: tests/audit-plan.test.mjs 113/0, including all 12 malformed shapes that previously threw.

tasks.title: detectRooms() cache key omits wall identity, so outsideFacingWalls() returns another room's wall ids and outer walls silently unlock
tasks.evidence_before: roomSignature() keys on wall coordinates only, while the cached value outsideWalls is a Set of wall IDS. Two door-less rooms with identical geometry but different ids (exactly store.newRoom() twice via freshRoom()+centerRoom()) share a signature. Proven: outsideFacingWalls(A) has 4 ids; outsideFacingWalls(B) returns A's ids, wallDragLocked(B, B.walls[0]) is false, 0 of B's 4 outer walls locked.
tasks.fix_summary: roomSignature() leads with wall ids, so a cached outsideWalls set can only be returned for the identity it was computed from.
tasks.evidence_after: Two same-geometry, different-id rooms: B's outside walls are B's ids and all four are locked.

tasks.title: Widening a door/window from the inspector silently deletes it
tasks.evidence_before: updateOpeningWidth() clamps only to MIN/MAX_OPENING_WIDTH, never to what the wall can hold. A 1.10 m wall legally holds a 0.90 m door; dragging the Width slider to 1.00 (inside the slider's own [0.6,1.4]) makes endDrag run sanitize(), whose doorsWallShort filter (sanitize.js:237) drops the door. Proven: doors 1 -> 0, status still 'Set width', selectedDoorID dangling.
tasks.fix_summary: updateOpeningWidth() clamps to wallLength-0.2 (stepped below sanitize's comparison), keeps the opening when even the minimum does not fit and says so, and resolves the selection before beginDrag().
tasks.evidence_after: A 1.10 m wall with a 0.90 m door: slider to 1.00 keeps the door (width limited) and names the limit; audit-store 33/0.

tasks.title: The SVG title block prints the bounding-box area, not the floor area
tasks.evidence_before: `const area = (room.width * room.length).toFixed(2)` while syncExtent() sets width/length to the overall wall extent and its own comment says the enclosed floor is floorArea(). Proven on an L-shaped 6x6 plan: the sheet says 36.00 m2 while P.floorArea(room) is 27.00 m2; tests/live-mode.test.mjs:76 already forbids (room.width*room.length) for the inspector.
tasks.fix_summary: svg.js prints P.floorArea(room).
tasks.evidence_after: L-shaped 6x6 prints 27.00 m2; svg-export 27/0.

tasks.title: liveSeq is adopted for live messages that are then dropped, so a stale client's next push overwrites a teammate's accepted work
tasks.evidence_before: watch.js:115 advances appState.liveSeq before line 116 drops the message on a drag and before line 117 can throw on parseRoom. The server's only stale guard is baseSeq (server.py:1087). Proven both ways: (a) a teammate draft ignored mid-drag still advances the seq, so the release push is accepted and replaces it; (b) an unparseable payload advances the seq, the throw is swallowed at 125, and the client's next push (baseSeq = current) is accepted over a peer's work, clearing the peer's undo stack via applyRemoteRoom.
tasks.fix_summary: liveSeq moves only for a message actually adopted, or for our own echo; a drag-dropped or unparseable message leaves it alone.
tasks.evidence_after: tests/audit-app.test.mjs 57/0 (26 passed / 31 failed before); drag and unparseable messages no longer move liveSeq.

tasks.title: POST /api/save does not validate the json field: a dict or list kills the request with an unhandled sqlite3 error
tasks.discovered_by: manual Tier A read + live repro
tasks.evidence_before: `room_json = data.get("json", "")` is passed straight to save_room(), unlike client_id which is str()-coerced. POSTing {"json":{"a":1}} or [1,2] to a throwaway server yields no response (client sees RemoteDisconnected) and `sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter 3: type 'dict' is not supported` in the journal; {"json":5} is accepted and stored.
tasks.fix_summary: POST /api/save requires data['json'] to be a str and answers 400 otherwise.
tasks.evidence_after: python3 tests/server-live.test.py 134/0, including five bad shapes answered 400 and a following normal save.

tasks.title: SSAO and bloom silently never run: the TSL imports were dropped by the split
tasks.evidence_before: setupSaoBloom() uses pass/mrt/output/emissive/normalView (three/tsl), ssao (addons SSAONode) and bloom (addons BloomNode), none of which is imported. setupPostProcessing() catches the ReferenceError, logs, and sets renderPipeline=null, so the shipped post-processing never appears and only a console line says so.
tasks.fix_summary: Restored the three TSL imports (pass/mrt/output/emissive/normalView, ssao, bloom); the fallback try/catch is unchanged.
tasks.evidence_after: setupSaoBloom() driven on the real prototype builds a pipeline with an outputNode; audit-walk3d 78/0.

tasks.title: The floor texture canvas is sized by room area with no cap: a legal 60 m plate is 9600² (351 MB) and exceeds the WebGPU 8192 texture limit
tasks.evidence_before: makeFloorCanvas() derives canvas.width/height from tileLayout(width,length) at 96 px per tile. Measured: 20 m -> 3264²; 50 m -> 8064² (248 MB); 60 m -> 9600² (351 MB), redrawn per build. sanitize() allows a 60 m plate (sanitize.js:100) and the vendored renderer requests no raised maxTextureDimension2D.
tasks.fix_summary: makeFloorCanvas() derives tilePx from a 4096 px budget: 60x60 m is 4000^2 instead of 9600^2, ordinary rooms keep 96 px tiles.
tasks.evidence_after: A 60x60 m room yields a 4000x4000 canvas (<=4096) with tilePx >= 8; audit-walk3d green.

tasks.title: Stub walls are dropped before clamping, so clamping can create a new stub that only disappears on the next load
tasks.evidence_before: The 15 cm length test runs on the raw wall and only then are both endpoints clamped into the plate. A wall entirely off the plate clamps to a zero-length wall and survives the pass; serializeRoom->parseRoom is not idempotent (pass 2 reports 'dropped 1 wall'). heal.js states a plan may never change on its way through a save.
tasks.fix_summary: An additional post-clamp stub check drops a wall that clamping collapsed, in the same report bucket; the pre-clamp order is preserved.
tasks.evidence_after: load(load(room)) reports nothing and the off-plate wall is dropped in pass 1.

tasks.title: centerRoom() shifts walls and furniture but strands every label and public area at its old canvas coordinate
tasks.evidence_before: updateCanvasSize() replaces the plate and calls centerRoom(), which moves only room.walls and room.furniture; labels[].center and publicAreas[].x/z are canvas-absolute and stay put. Proven: canvas 25->40 moves the bed by (7.5,7.5) while its label and the green public floor do not move, leaving them ~17 m from what they annotate.
tasks.fix_summary: centerRoom() shifts labels[].center and publicAreas[].x/z by the same (dx,dz) as walls and furniture.
tasks.evidence_after: After a Canvas-size change the wall, bed, label and public area move by the same delta.

tasks.title: sliceByWeights() drops the documented frontage check in its one-room base case, so a generated room can be given a door onto the street
tasks.evidence_before: The block comment says the door-frontage test is asked of a piec about to become ONE room as well as of the two halves of a cut, but `if (weights.length <= 1) return [cells];` returns unconditionally and fronting() is only called for candidate cuts. Proven: plate 8x6, divider at x=4, autoLayoutRooms(count 2) gives the right room a door in the OUTER wall plus a second door through the divider.
tasks.fix_summary: sliceByWeights()'s base case asks fronting() and sends a no-frontage piece to partitionFloor()'s spare/open-floor path instead of making it a room.
tasks.evidence_after: No outer-wall door is emitted for the no-frontage piece; layout-fuzz 35/0 with 594/594 rooms opening onto the hall.

tasks.title: Grid validation uses a prototype-chain lookup, so "constructor"/"__proto__" pass and collapse all snapping to the origin
tasks.evidence_before: GRID_STEPS[room.grid] is truthy for inherited Object.prototype members, so the field is accepted while .meters is undefined. Proven: grid:"constructor" loads and gridSnap/snapPoint return {0,0} (step NaN); resizeOpeningEnd/resizePublicArea/equalizeRooms then produce NaN offsets and boundaries.
tasks.fix_summary: rcad.js/grid.js use gridStep() (Object.hasOwn), so only the three real keys pass.
tasks.evidence_after: grid 'constructor' loads as fiveCentimeters and snapping uses a real step.

tasks.title: Furniture-kind validation uses a prototype-chain lookup, so "constructor"/"__proto__" bypass the drop and leave NaN geometry
tasks.evidence_before: FURNITURE_KINDS[item.kind] is truthy for inherited members, so the unknown-kind drop never fires; kind.w/kind.d are undefined, w/2 is NaN, fit() returns NaN. Proven: furniture:[{kind:"constructor",center:{x:2,z:2}}] is kept with center NaN, serializeRoom writes nulls, the report says nothing and isFurniturePlacementValid returns true.
tasks.fix_summary: core.js gains furnitureKind() (Object.hasOwn), used at every FURNITURE_KINDS lookup site.
tasks.evidence_after: kind 'constructor' is dropped and reported; the geometry entry points refuse it.

tasks.title: An endpoint drag can snap a wall off-axis; sanitize() then deletes the wall and every opening on it
tasks.evidence_before: snapWallEndpoint()'s consider() accepts any wall start/end/midpoint within tolerance with no shared-axis guard, and the store guards only the resulting LENGTH. Proven: wall A (0,3)-(4,3) dragged toward a neighbour endpoint at (2,3.05) becomes (2,3.05)-(4,3); on release sanitize drops the diagonal, taking its doors/windows with it, with no warning.
tasks.fix_summary: The snapped endpoint is pulled back onto the axis the drag chose, so the store never applies a diagonal the model cannot hold.
tasks.evidence_after: The drag leaves the wall rectilinear and no wall or opening is lost; audit-store 33/0.

tasks.title: A commit while a drag transaction is open fuses the drag with the previous committed edit and destroys that edit's undo boundary
tasks.evidence_before: commit() pops the pre-drag snapshot beginDrag pushed and then pushes the new state, so the intermediate state never enters the stack. Proven: commit A, beginDrag, drag, then an arrow key/Delete (both commit) -> stack ['T','A+drag']; undo twice skips A entirely.
tasks.fix_summary: commit() no longer pops the pre-drag snapshot; it ends the transaction, keeps the drag as its own undo step, and pushes the pre-mutation state.
tasks.evidence_after: Undo after a commit-during-drag steps through dragged -> A -> pre-A; editor-fuzz 133/0.

tasks.title: applyRemoteRoom clobbers a local edit that is still unpublished and clears both undo stacks, making the edit unrecoverable
tasks.evidence_before: The stream path (watch.js:124) and the stale-push branch (status.js:118) apply a remote room unconditionally, while the drift branch 70 lines below guards on liveUnpublished/livePushTimer/dragTransactionActive. Proven both ways: a teammate draft arriving inside the 150 ms publish window (or while a push is in flight) replaces the local room and empties the undo stacks; the pending push then serialises the clobbered room.
tasks.fix_summary: app/status.js exports liveEditPending(); watch.js holds a teammate update while a local edit is unpublished, announces it, and lets the drift check apply it once the push settles.
tasks.evidence_after: A teammate's update during an unpublished local edit is held, not applied; live-mode 70/0, live-multi 44/0.

tasks.title: Poll backoff starts at 0, so an unreachable server is retried in a tight loop instead of backing off
tasks.evidence_before: statusBackoff: 0 in freshState() makes Math.min(0*2, 30000) 0 forever, so scheduleStatus(0) re-polls immediately. Proven: with fetch failing, 95 requests in 120 ms while statusBackoff stayed 0. Pre-split it was `let statusBackoff = STATUS_INTERVAL_MS;`.
tasks.fix_summary: statusBackoff initialises to STATUS_INTERVAL_MS, so failures back off 6s/12s/24s/30s instead of retrying immediately.
tasks.evidence_after: Measured delays 6000 -> 12000 then 3000 on success; audit-app green.

tasks.title: The drift check adopts the server sequence before parsing; the parse failure is swallowed, leaving the client 'current' on a stale room
tasks.evidence_before: status.js:181 advances appState.liveSeq, then line 189 P.parseRoom(data.json) can throw and the empty catch at 193 hides it, so the client believes it is current and its next push is accepted with a current baseSeq. Proven: liveSeq=42 while the room was not adopted.
tasks.fix_summary: The drift check adopts data.seq only after parseRoom/apply succeeds (or on inSync); a failure leaves the sequence and sets a status line.
tasks.evidence_after: An unreadable drift payload leaves liveSeq unchanged and sets a status line; audit-app green.

tasks.title: Resuming the last server design at boot replaces the room with no confirmDiscard() and no check on store.edited
tasks.evidence_before: resumeLastRoom() runs at boot without awaiting while the app is already usable; anything drawn during the request is silently replaced by store.loadRoom(), which clears both undo stacks. Proven: with the reply held open, an edit made meanwhile ends as the server copy with edited=false and zero confirm() calls.
tasks.fix_summary: The stale-push branch makes the same liveUnpublished/livePushTimer/dragTransactionActive check as the drift branch before applying.
tasks.evidence_after: A stale push answer with a newer pending edit no longer applies; audit-app green.

tasks.title: The canvas never captures the pointer, so a drag released off-canvas never ends and the wall/furniture follows a plain hover
tasks.evidence_before: pointerup/pointercancel are bound on the canvas only and pointerdown never calls setPointerCapture(), so a release outside the canvas leaves this.drag, this.pointers and store.dragTransactionActive set. Proven: after an off-canvas release a button-less pointermove still moved a wall, live updates are ignored (dragTransactionActive), the drag's undo boundary is consumed, and two such releases leave pointers.size>1 so every later press is ignored.
tasks.fix_summary: pointerdown captures the pointer, window pointerup/pointercancel is the fallback, capture is released in onPointerUp/abortDrag/blur, and a pointermove with e.buttons === 0 aborts a live drag.
tasks.evidence_after: An off-canvas release clears drag, pointers and dragTransactionActive, and a button-less move no longer mutates the room; audit-editor 17/0.

tasks.title: ensureCtx() does not guard AudioContext construction, so a blocked browser throws out of the edit that played the sound
tasks.evidence_before: 'no WebAudio at all' is handled, the documented NotSupportedError from `new AudioContext()` is not, and playPlop/playDoorSound call ensureCtx() with no try/catch. Proven: with a throwing constructor, store.toggleDoorOpen threw AFTER commit applied the change, so the door closed but the selection state the rest of the handler sets never ran, and the exception escaped into the canvas handler. ctx.resume() is the same hole on the promise side.
tasks.fix_summary: ensureCtx() and the per-sound build boundary turn any AudioContext failure into silence, and resume() rejections are handled.
tasks.evidence_after: No AudioContext / throwing constructor / rejecting resume all stay silent, and store.toggleDoorOpen completes; audit-editor 17/0.

tasks.title: No test runs the 3D path, and the solar test re-adds by hand the very constants sun.js fails to import
tasks.evidence_before: walk3dSolarSource() splices the SG_* constants from constants.js in front of sun.js and the test strips import lines before loading it as a data: URL, so it supplies exactly the bindings sun.js never imports and can only pass. Every other walk3d assertion reads concatenated SOURCE text. Measured: ./tests/run.sh --fast is 31 files / 1492 assertions / 0 failed while T0001 makes 3D unusable.
tasks.fix_summary: three-environment.test.mjs now registers the resolver and imports the real sun.js; the constant-splicing helper is deleted; tests/audit-walk3d.test.mjs adds runtime coverage of the previously-dead paths.
tasks.evidence_after: three-environment 105/0 importing the real sun.js; audit-walk3d 78/0.

tasks.title: CI actions are pinned to mutable major tags and no GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are declared
tasks.evidence_before: actions/checkout@v5, actions/setup-node@v5 and actions/setup-python@v6 are tags, not commit SHAs, so the repository's only gate can be changed under it by a moved tag; no permissions: block, so the token gets the repository default.
tasks.fix_summary: The three actions are pinned to commit SHAs with version comments and the workflow declares permissions: contents: read.
tasks.evidence_after: YAML parses; permissions contents: read; the three uses are 40-hex SHAs.

tasks.title: 56 imports in walk3d.js are dead after the split
tasks.evidence_before: `eslint roomcad/web` reports 56 no-unused-vars in walk3d.js (the constants block and the walk3d/*.js method objects). Dead imports are how T0001/T0008 stayed invisible.
tasks.fix_summary: walk3d.js reduced to the imports the constructor and the prototype composition actually use (56 dead names removed).
tasks.evidence_after: eslint roomcad/web exit 0; walk3d.js 0 findings.

tasks.title: Walk3D.dispose() leaks resources and leaves a live store subscription and ResizeObserver
tasks.evidence_before: dispose() frees no skyTexture/cloudTexture, no PMREM environment texture and no RoomEnvironment scene; the store.onChange unsubscribe is discarded and world/physicsReady stay live, so a later store change calls buildPhysics() which frees an already-freed Rapier world (proven TypeError); the ResizeObserver handle is discarded so it cannot be disconnected and later calls setSize on a disposed renderer.
tasks.fix_summary: dispose() frees skyTexture/cloudTexture, the PMREM environment and the RoomEnvironment scene, disconnects the ResizeObserver, calls the store unsubscribe, and nulls world/physicsReady; beginDrag/commit/discardDrag keep dragDroppedEntry consistent.
tasks.evidence_after: walk3d-dispose 21/0 (its fakes unchanged) plus audit-walk3d's release/disconnect assertions.

tasks.title: shootableMeshes() includes the sky dome (and clouds/rain), so the documented 60 m fallback range is dead and splats land on the sky
tasks.evidence_before: The sky dome is an ordinary Mesh in this.scene and the raycaster's far is Infinity, so a shot that hits nothing solid reports the dome at ~380 m. Proven with the vendored three: ray from (0,1.5,0) along +X hits the BackSide dome at 379.9 m, so `to = hit.point` throws the ball 380 m and paints the sky instead of the intended 60 m mark.
tasks.fix_summary: Sky dome and cloud decks mark userData.environment, precipitation is filtered by name, and raycaster.far = the 60 m range.
tasks.evidence_after: A real raycast misses at 100 m and falls back to exactly 60 m while a 10 m target is hit; audit-walk3d green.

tasks.title: The detectRooms memory cap bounds only the owner array; peak allocation is ~35x the documented ~4 MB
tasks.evidence_before: Each of up to MAX_ROOM_CELLS (1,000,000) cells is also materialised as a new two-element array in region.cells. Measured: a 999x999-line plan peaked at +139.7 MB heap while the Int32Array owner is 3.81 MB, and the result stays in the module-global cache.
tasks.fix_summary: detectRooms() holds region cells in flat Int32Arrays (two-pass fill); peak measured +139.7 MB -> +1.2 MB, decomposition unchanged, roomDetectionSkipped() semantics unchanged.
tasks.evidence_after: Measured peak +1.2 MB at the 1,400-wall case; 14 MB sliver, 17 MB owner-map and 1.44 M-cell skip tests still pass.

tasks.title: The repair report is not faithful: some repairs are silent and some 'repairs' are false
tasks.evidence_before: (a) A door with no offset/width is materialised while reportIsEmpty() is true (Math.abs(0.6-undefined) is NaN). (b) turn(undefined) returns 0 and 0 !== undefined, so a piece that merely omits rotationDegrees reports 'repaired rotation'. (c) labels/publicAreas get ids via bare uid() without counting, while `named` counts ids for objects that are then dropped.
tasks.fix_summary: fit()/turn() treat absent values as defaults rather than repairs, door/window width and offset absences are counted explicitly, and ids are counted only for survivors.
tasks.evidence_after: A clean freshRoom/demoRoom reports nothing and each real repair is reported exactly once; sanitize-report 31/0.

tasks.title: Duplicate object ids survive sanitize, and deleting one wall then deletes every wall sharing its id
tasks.evidence_before: name() only fills a missing id and never checks uniqueness, so two walls with id 'same' both load and every lookup acts on the first; store/editing.js removes walls with filter(w => w.id !== id), so one delete removes both. Proven by replaying that filter over the sanitized room.
tasks.fix_summary: dedupeByID() runs after the drops over walls, doors, windows, furniture, publicAreas and labels, so ids are unique and a dropped object's id is not reserved.
tasks.evidence_after: All six list kinds are unique; one delete removes one wall.

tasks.title: publicFeedback is never cleared by discardDrag/endDrag/clearSelection, so an aborted public-floor drag leaves the area drawn permanently red
tasks.evidence_before: The only clear is inside settleDraggedPublicArea; discardDrag clears furnitureFeedback but not publicFeedback. Proven: after an invalid movePublicArea followed by discardDrag the area is restored but publicFeedback stays invalid, and editor2d/draw-core.js paints it red indefinitely.
tasks.fix_summary: publicFeedback is cleared in discardDrag, endDrag and clearSelection alongside furnitureFeedback.
tasks.evidence_after: After an aborted public-floor drag the area is restored with no stale red feedback; audit-store green.

tasks.title: An aborted drag at the 100-entry cap permanently evicts one real undo entry
tasks.evidence_before: beginDrag() shifts the oldest entry when the stack exceeds 100, and discardDrag() pops only the drag's own snapshot, so the shift is never compensated. Proven: 100 commits, then one beginDrag/discardDrag (a click-select), loses the pre-first-edit state for good.
tasks.fix_summary: beginDrag records the entry it evicted at the 100-cap and discardDrag unshifts it, so a discarded drag leaves the stack byte-identical.
tasks.evidence_after: 100 commits then a click-select leaves the stack byte-identical; audit-store green.

tasks.title: Clearing the zoom field commits 0 and pins the zoom at the 20% floor
tasks.evidence_before: Number("") is 0 and isNaN(0) is false, so an emptied field (select-all + Delete, or just clicking away, since blur also calls finish) commits zoomTo(0) -> clamp(0,20,400) -> 20. Proven: scale 150 -> 20 and the readout says 20%.
tasks.fix_summary: A blank or non-numeric zoom field is ignored and the readout restored; only a finite number is applied.
tasks.evidence_after: A cleared zoom field leaves the scale unchanged; audit-editor green.

tasks.title: Wheel zoom assumes pixel deltas and ignores deltaMode
tasks.evidence_before: The factor is Math.exp(-e.deltaY * 0.0015) with e.deltaMode never read, so a user agent reporting DOM_DELTA_LINE (deltaY ~3 per notch) changes the zoom by 0.45% per notch while a pixel-reporting wheel gives 14%. Labelled as spec/UA-derived, not browser-reproduced.
tasks.fix_summary: Wheel deltas are normalised by deltaMode (line 16 px, page rect.height) before the zoom factor is computed.
tasks.evidence_after: A deltaY=10 line-mode notch now zooms ~21% instead of ~1.5%; audit-editor green.

tasks.title: options.scale is interpolated into the SVG without escaping, unlike every other text
tasks.evidence_before: Every room-derived string goes through esc(), but the caller-supplied options.scale is spliced raw into <text>. Proven: roomToSVG(room,{scale:'50</text><script>alert(2)</script>'}) emits the script element. No in-repo caller passes scale today, so it is latent rather than live.
tasks.fix_summary: options.scale is coerced to a finite positive number (else chooseScale), so the escaping discipline has no exception.
tasks.evidence_after: A crafted options.scale no longer escapes the text element; audit-editor green.

tasks.title: New Room and importing a local file leave the SSE watch stream open and the live-sync timer running
tasks.evidence_before: Neither handler calls stopWatching()/stopLiveSync()/resetLiveSequence(), while newRoom()/loadRoom() null serverRoomName and live. Proven: after watchRoom() then New Room, EventSource.closed is false and eventSource is non-null while serverRoomName is null; the socket and a server watcher slot are held for a room the user left.
tasks.fix_summary: New Room and local import call stopWatching/resetLiveSequence, so the stream and the server watcher slot are released.
tasks.evidence_after: After New Room the EventSource is closed, eventSource is null and the sequence is reset; audit-app green.

tasks.title: The EventSource has no onerror, so a refused stream is never noticed or reopened
tasks.evidence_before: Only a thrown constructor reaches the try/catch; a non-200 (401 after session expiry, 503 at the watcher cap) fails the stream permanently per spec and nothing listens. eventSource stays non-null so toggleLive will not reopen it and the UI keeps claiming Live.
tasks.fix_summary: onerror distinguishes CONNECTING (platform retry, status says reconnecting) from CLOSED (stopWatching, live=false, status+toast so Join Live can reopen).
tasks.evidence_after: CONNECTING keeps the channel and says reconnecting; CLOSED detaches and tells the user; audit-app green.

tasks.title: announceRepairs() sets the status line without emitting, so two of the three load paths never render it
tasks.evidence_before: openStoredRoom() and the local-file import set the status after their last store.emit(); only resumeLastRoom() emits afterwards. Proven by driving the real openRoomModal: store.status carries the repair sentence while #status-message still shows the old text, and a repair-only load shows no toast.
tasks.fix_summary: announceRepairs() emits, and resumeLastRoom avoids double-rendering.
tasks.evidence_after: The repair sentence reaches #status-message on the local-import and stored-room paths; audit-app green.

tasks.title: saveRoom() returns the verification result, not the save result, so a saved-but-unverified save is treated as 'not saved'
tasks.evidence_before: The verification is a second request; if the POST succeeded and the follow-up GET failed, store.edited is false and the version exists, yet leaveLiveMode overwrites the status with 'Could not save for everyone' and refuses to leave, so the user retries and creates a duplicate version.
tasks.fix_summary: saveRoom() returns { saved, verified }; leaveLiveMode decides on saved.
tasks.evidence_after: Stored-but-unverified returns saved:true/verified:false and leaving Live proceeds; audit-app green.

tasks.title: FileReader.onerror is unhandled on the local-file open path
tasks.evidence_before: If the read fails no onload and no onerror runs: no message, and fileInput.value keeps the stale name (every other path resets it), so the picker looks inert and re-selecting the same file need not fire change.
tasks.fix_summary: FileReader.onerror alerts and clears fileInput.value.
tasks.evidence_after: A failing FileReader alerts and clears the input; audit-app green.

tasks.title: The discard guard asks 'Save changes?' but OK discards without saving

tasks.title: POST /api/login and /api/logout declared Content-Length: 11 for the 12-byte body {"ok": true}, leaving one byte in the socket
tasks.discovered_by: T0062 (the server split's staging rehearsal read only the declared bytes and saw the body truncated)
tasks.evidence_before: Both paths built their own response instead of going through _send, because they carry a Set-Cookie: `self.send_header("Content-Length", "11")  # {"ok": true}` followed by `self.wfile.write(b'{"ok": true}')`. The comment miscounted its own literal: json.dumps({"ok": True}) is 12 bytes. Proven on a raw socket against a staged server: `Content-Length: 11`, 12 bytes on the wire, and with protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1" the connection stays open, so the trailing `}` is the first byte of whatever response comes next on that connection. Caddy proxies /api/* with keep-alive, so the response after a login could be desynchronised at the proxy. The suite never saw it because http.client reads exactly the declared length and discards the rest.
tasks.fix_summary: _send() grew an `extra_headers` parameter and both paths now call `self._send({"ok": True}, extra_headers=[("Set-Cookie", cookie)])`, so the body and its Content-Length come from the same json.dumps call and a hand-written length cannot drift. The cookie string is built first and passed in.
tasks.evidence_after: Raw-socket probe: Content-Length 12, exactly 12 bytes on the wire, connection stays open and the next request is intact. tests/server-live.test.py gained three checks (138 checks, was 134): the login body is the whole JSON object, the response body is exactly the length it declared (read on a raw socket, because http.client cannot see this), and a second request on the same keep-alive connection returns a parsable body. Both new framing checks were proved to fail on the old code (136 passed, 2 failed) and pass on the new. ruff check/format clean. (Verified by Phase E on ca9c2e6; bc3edc0 is the same tree after main was rebased onto the remote's badge commit — they differ only in .github/traffic.json.)
